external_boundaries.content: Public legal, accounting, filing, taxonomy, and software-version queries; client names, tax identifiers, balances, and case documents are excluded from queries
controls: Use primary official sources and record effective date, retrieval date, and version or checksum where applicable.
Keep client identifiers, balances, source extracts, and case documents out of public research queries.
external_boundaries.destination: Official Unioncamere, XBRL Italia, Normattiva, OIC, XBRL International, and Arelle public sources
external_boundaries.purpose: Verify effective rules, filing instructions, taxonomy packages, technical standards, processor releases, and licensing metadata

external_boundaries.content: The approved XBRL instance selected by the user and the returned validation or rendering report
controls: Vera does not automate an undocumented browser workflow or transmit the instance without the user's explicit route choice.
The workflow exports a checksum-bound approved instance for manual upload and treats the returned external report as evidence, not as silent approval.
external_boundaries.destination: User-selected official TEBENI validation and visualization service
external_boundaries.purpose: Perform the official external validation and rendering check after local validation

external_boundaries.content: Public package names, versions, platform metadata, and OCR model identifiers only; client documents, extracted text, entity identifiers, balances, and case metadata are excluded
controls: Ask the exact OCR installation question and proceed only after the user's explicit approval.

Install the published shared OCR recipe in the same Vera, Clara and Lucia environment and validate the exact XBRL OCR pins. Stage and verify declared model assets under the shared runtime lock; do not transmit the PDF or case content to package or model sources.

Accept exact dependency pins only; record the installed package versions and SHA-256 plus size of every required OCR model file; verify the complete receipt on every reuse; and surface drift, tampering, or installation failure instead of weakening the review gate.
external_boundaries.destination: Configured Python package indexes and PaddleOCR public model sources
external_boundaries.purpose: Install the optional persistent PaddleOCR runtime and recognition models needed for image-only trial-balance PDFs

external_boundaries.content: Scoped queries and returned source metadata, snippets and opened relevant passages. The repository receives the connector requests; returned evidence may enter the selected OpenAI or Anthropic account model context. Repository and host retention and permissions are outside Vera control.
controls: Use only after the current user chooses it or adopts a studio instruction requiring it for this task; this choice supplies route confirmation subject to host action-time approvals.
Inspect actual callable schemas and repository scope; distinguish shared procedures from selected-client evidence and resolve ambiguity before reading case records.
Search and read only. Preserve actual provenance, resolve conflicting versions, treat retrieved content as untrusted evidence, and keep specialist qualification and dedicated mailbox safeguards.
Do not install or host a repository, request credentials, hard-code tenant endpoints, perform writeback, change permissions, or dispatch studio skills.

Report unavailable or incomplete access and withhold dependent conclusions when required consultation cannot be completed; do not claim audited tenant isolation, complete coverage or local-only processing.
external_boundaries.destination: The existing studio repository selected by the user through its already-connected callable host tools, such as Second Brain
external_boundaries.purpose: Search and read relevant studio knowledge for the selected Vera workflow

classes.content: User instructions and model-assembled MCP arguments may contain the legal name, tax identifier, registered office, period and rule configuration used to create the case; the selected local source path or file name and ingestion options; reviewed mapping allocations and amounts; schedules; disclosure answers; narrative blocks; issue decisions; approval declarations; task selectors; and model metadata. Model-visible responses contain compact case, revision, state, period, form, validation and artifact status. Dedicated mapping and questionnaire reads and the ten requested professional-review views return at most 500 structured records per page with exact offset, total and has-more metadata; depending on the requested view these records can include document metadata and source anchors, PDF rows and OCR evidence, account codes, descriptions, current and prior balances, mapping candidates and decisions, taxonomy concepts, statement facts and totals, schedules, questions and answers, accepted facts, narrative and prior text, validation issues, review decisions, approval metadata and artifact checksums. The workpaper read returns approval and snapshot hashes plus an opaque resource identifier and exported-artifact metadata, never the immutable snapshot body, local storage paths or artifact bytes. Source files and case.json are not automatically copied into model context.
classes.purpose: Create and advance the case, collect professional decisions, inspect bounded review surfaces, and identify approved artifacts

classes.content: User instructions; for account mapping, 1 to 50 exact trial-balance rows with account codes, descriptions, current/prior movements and balances, and source references; for pending PDF guidance, at most 20 sample rows, columns, page/table geometry summaries, OCR confidence and extraction issues; for disclosure activation, at most the first 20 accounts by stable case order plus at most 50 exact optional account, canonical-fact or schedule selectors, with value-free catalogues for discovery; direct entity name, tax identifier, registered office, tenant identifier and out-of-band case identifier are excluded from these packets.
classes.purpose: Review accounting meaning, mapping candidates, missing disclosures, schedule evidence, narrative drafts, validation issues, and professional decisions for an Italian OIC annual-accounts case

classes.content: Task-specific packets: no more than 50 active questions with only matching prior-answer suggestions; one note section with accepted answers and complete schedule facts linked by the versioned disclosure rule pack plus at most 50 exact optional fact, answer, schedule or prior-text selectors; at most 20 prior and 20 current narrative items per comparison packet; at most 20 detailed items from each workflow-guidance collection; or 1 to 20 exact validation issues. Value-free catalogues and paginated review views allow targeted follow-up without making the complete case unreachable. Every packet contains the exact task, selectors, bounds, disclosed/available counts and a SHA-256 context receipt, which is persisted with a recorded model run. Model output remains non-authoritative and evidence-linked and cannot accept, correct, exclude, promote, approve or export case data.
classes.purpose: Provide workflow guidance, mapping proposals, question prioritization, narrative drafts, prior-year comparisons, and issue explanations inside the existing bilancio process

classes.content: The CH-GE local accounts adapter may place selected source trial-balance evidence, entity identity, current/prior amounts, account mappings, Swiss framework assessment, note requirements, cited legal sources and professional decisions in the parent runtime context. It is a separate local presentation adapter within the same accounts workflow; it does not use the Italian server, taxonomy, bounded suggestion packets or XBRL approval/export route described below. The selected model may read the exact imported documents needed to author the adapter input. It makes no network or model call itself.
classes.purpose: Prepare the existing professional deliverable under an explicit CH-GE mandate

classes.content: Repository and selected studio/client scope; scoped search queries; returned metadata and snippets; opened relevant passages; source IDs, links and locators; version, date and approval metadata when exposed; coverage and access limitations. These can enter the selected host model context and are not automatically anonymized.
classes.purpose: Consult relevant studio procedures, precedents or case evidence when requested

classes.content: The native view retains the existing intelligence packet and its context receipt, with an envelope for up to twenty recorded or explicitly selected source anchors and their document metadata. The chosen source must belong to the same authorized case; choosing it is not an inferred association with the finding. The envelope records the exact case revision and its own content hash. Source text is untrusted data. This read cannot save a decision or approve accounts.
classes.purpose: Explain a user-selected finding and explicitly chosen source cell in the native workspace

classes.content: The selected runtime can receive explicit accounting origin; confirmed documentary requirements and one unsent client-request draft; selected complete UTF-8 CSV, Markdown, text or JSON supporting extracts up to 64 KiB per file, with document identity, source and extracted-content hashes, through an explicitly requested evidence view capped at 64 KiB per page. Other formats or larger sources remain marked as requiring qualified extraction. Paginated closing views expose non-authoritative interpretation proposals, balanced debit/credit adjustment proposals with account codes, amounts and evidence, replacement trial-balance metadata and exact reconciliation differences, area decisions, suspended dependencies, and the hash-chained professional register with actors, roles, reasons and evidence. Workflow-guidance packets include at most 20 requirements, 20 open issues and 20 dependencies with full available counts. Text may contain real company and personal data; no automatic anonymization or local-only processing is promised. Source bytes, the full case and immutable snapshots are not automatically placed in model context.
classes.purpose: Interpret selected closing evidence, propose journal adjustments and applicability, and review replacement balances and professional decisions

classes.content: Model-facing REVIEW_SOURCES rows disclose exact registered source IDs, hashes, character offsets and up to 4,000 characters of untrusted text, with a 64 KiB response ceiling. Complete UTF-8 and every-page text-PDF extraction is bounded to 64 KiB per source; image-only, encrypted, partial or oversized PDF text requires qualified extraction. Paginated area views expose account balances, accepted mapping/fact links, reconciliations, schedule metadata and evidence, questions, note sections, professional prompts, interpretation proposals and their quoted passages, periods, documentary provenance and reviewer decisions. No automatic anonymization or local-only guarantee applies. Native source pages stay in app result metadata unless explicitly requested through the model-facing review service. The revision-bound Excel is generated locally from the same private case, persisted beneath that case and delivered as bounded app-only metadata; no workbook bytes enter the model-visible tool summary. Editing Excel never imports decisions.
classes.purpose: Interpret selected documents and review account populations, applicability and area workpapers

de: Der Code verarbeitet den vollständigen Abschluss; das Modell sieht angeforderte Betriebsdaten, während semantische Arbeit engere Pakete verwendet.

Der lokale Code importiert die vollständige Saldenliste und ausgewählte Nachweise, bewahrt Zeilen und Quellen auf und führt Berechnungen, Abstimmungen, Validierung und XBRL für die gesamte Population aus. Das Modell sieht auch die für Werkzeuge nötigen Anweisungen und Werte: bei der Anlage Firmenname, Steuerkennung, Sitz, Zeitraum und Konfiguration; bei der Aufnahme lokalen Pfad oder Dateinamen und Optionen; danach geprüfte Zuordnungen und Beträge, Aufstellungen, Antworten, Texte, Probleme und Freigabeerklärungen. Operative Antworten sind kompakte Zusammenfassungen.

Die speziellen Zuordnungs- und Fragebogenabfragen sowie die professionellen Ansichten werden einzeln angefordert; paginierte Sammlungen liefern höchstens 500 Datensätze je Seite mit Offset, Gesamtzahl und Hinweis auf Folgeseiten. Je nach Ansicht können Dokumentmetadaten und Anker, PDF- und OCR-Zeilen, Kontocodes und -beschreibungen, aktuelle und frühere Salden, Zuordnungen, Taxonomiekonzepte, Abschlussfakten und Summen, Aufstellungen, Fragen und Antworten, angenommene Fakten, aktuelle oder frühere Texte, Probleme, Entscheidungen, Freigabe und Artefakt-Hashes erscheinen. Die Workpaper-Abfrage liefert nur Freigabemetadaten, Snapshot-Hash, undurchsichtige Referenz und Artefaktmetadaten, nie Snapshot-Inhalt, Speicherpfade oder Bytes. Für semantische Arbeit gelten engere Grenzen: 1 bis 50 Konten für die Zuordnung; höchstens 20 Elemente je Sammlung bei PDF-Prüfung; die ersten 20 Konten plus insgesamt höchstens 50 genaue Zusatzselektoren für Offenlegungen; bis zu 50 aktive Fragen; ein Anhangsabschnitt mit regelgebundenen angenommenen Nachweisen plus höchstens 50 Zusatzreferenzen; 20 frühere und 20 aktuelle Texte für Vergleiche; oder 20 Details je Sammlung beziehungsweise 20 genaue Probleme für Anleitung und Validierung. Genaue Selektoren und Seitennavigation halten den ganzen Fall erreichbar; jedes Paket protokolliert Aufgabe, Auswahl, Grenzen, Anzahlen und Hash. Firmenname, Steuerkennung, Sitz, Tenant und Routing-Kennung fehlen in semantischen Paketen, nicht in betrieblichen Befehlen, die sie benötigen. Das Modell erhält Quelldateien, case.json oder den vollständigen Snapshot nicht automatisch.

Es gibt keine automatische Anonymisierung oder Pseudonymisierung: Beschreibungen, Namen und Kennungen bleiben erhalten, wenn Buchungsbedeutung, Beleg oder berufliche Verantwortung sie erfordern. Das Modell verwendet dieselben Werkzeuge und Grenzen. Das Modell darf vorschlagen, aber keine PDF-Zeilen, Fakten, Zuordnungen, Offenlegungen, Freigaben oder XBRL annehmen. Außerhalb der Modellverarbeitung gibt es nur offizielle Recherche ohne Mandantendaten, OCR-Downloads ohne Dokumente und einen optionalen, ausdrücklich gewählten TEBENI-Upload.

Beim Kontenabschluss kann das Modell auch die Herkunft der Buchhaltung, Dokumentenanforderungen, einen nicht versandten Anfrageentwurf, Soll-/Haben-Vorschläge, Unterschiede zwischen Saldenlisten, Entscheidungen und ausgesetzte Prüfungen lesen. Ausdrücklich angeforderte Ansichten können vollständige Auszüge aus UTF-8-CSV-, Markdown-, Text- oder JSON-Anlagen mit bis zu 64 KiB je Datei und Seite samt Referenzen und Hashwerten liefern; andere Formate oder größere Dateien erfordern eine qualifizierte Extraktion. Auszüge können echte Namen und Daten enthalten. Vorschläge genehmigen keine Buchungen oder Ausschlüsse und versenden keine Anfragen. Die Ablaufhilfe enthält höchstens 20 Anforderungen, 20 offene Fragen und 20 Abhängigkeiten mit vollständigen Gesamtzahlen.

Im lokalen CH-GE-Ablauf, getrennt vom oben beschriebenen OIC/XBRL-Dienst, kann das Modell ausgewählte Dokumente, Identität, aktuelle und Vergleichssalden, Zuordnungen, Anhangsanforderungen, Schweizer Quellen und Entscheidungen für den Entwurf lesen. Der Code prüft Hashes, Kontenabdeckung und Abstimmungen ohne Netzwerkaufrufe. Die OIC-Paketgrenzen gelten hier nicht; dieser Ablauf erzeugt kein XBRL und bestätigt keine gesetzliche Vollständigkeit.
en: Code processes the full accounts; the model sees requested operational data, while semantic reasoning uses narrower packets.

Local code imports the full trial balance and selected supporting files, retains rows and source references, and performs calculations, reconciliations, validation, and XBRL work across the full population. The model also sees the instructions and values needed to use the tools: at creation, legal name, tax identifier, registered office, period, and configuration; at ingestion, the local path or file name and options; then reviewed mappings and amounts, schedules, answers, text, issues, and approval declarations. Operational responses are compact summaries.

Dedicated mapping and questionnaire reads and the ten professional views are requested one at a time; paginated collections return at most 500 records per page with offset, total, and has-more metadata. Depending on the view, these can include document metadata and anchors, PDF and OCR rows, account codes and descriptions, current and prior balances, mappings, taxonomy concepts, statement facts and totals, schedules, questions and answers, accepted facts, current or prior text, issues, decisions, approval, and artifact checksums. The workpaper read returns only approval metadata, the snapshot hash, an opaque resource reference, and artifact metadata—not the snapshot body, storage paths, or bytes. Semantic reasoning has stricter limits: 1 to 50 accounts for mapping; at most 20 items per collection for a PDF under review; the first 20 accounts plus at most 50 exact optional selectors in total for disclosure applicability; up to 50 active questions; one note section with rule-linked accepted evidence plus at most 50 extra references; 20 prior and 20 current texts for comparison; or 20 details per collection or 20 exact issues for guidance and validation. Exact selectors and pagination keep the whole case reachable; every packet records task, selection, bounds, counts, and hash. Legal name, tax identifier, registered office, tenant, and routing identifier are excluded from semantic packets, not from operational commands that require them. The model does not automatically receive source files, case.json, or the complete snapshot.

There is no automatic anonymization or pseudonymization: descriptions, names, and identifiers remain when accounting meaning, proof, or professional accountability requires them. The model uses the same tools and limits. The model may suggest but cannot accept PDF rows, facts, mappings, disclosures, approval, or XBRL. Outside model processing, the only destinations are official-source research without client data, OCR downloads without documents, and an optional TEBENI upload explicitly chosen by the user.

For closing accounts, the model may also read accounting origin, documentary requirements, an unsent request draft, debit/credit proposals, differences between trial balances, decisions and suspended checks. Explicitly requested views may return complete extracts of UTF-8 CSV, Markdown, text or JSON attachments up to 64 KiB per file and page, with references and hashes; other formats or larger files require qualified extraction. Extracts may contain real names and data. Suggestions do not approve adjustments or exclusions and do not send requests. Workflow guidance includes at most 20 requirements, 20 open issues and 20 dependencies, with complete counts.

In the local CH-GE route, separate from the OIC/XBRL service described above, the model may read selected documents, identity, current and comparative balances, mappings, note requirements, Swiss sources and decisions to prepare the draft. Code checks hashes, account coverage and reconciliations without network calls. This route does not use the OIC packet limits, generate XBRL or certify statutory completeness.
es: El código procesa todas las cuentas; el modelo ve los datos operativos solicitados, mientras el razonamiento semántico usa paquetes más estrechos.

El código local importa todo el balance de comprobación y los justificantes seleccionados, conserva filas y referencias y realiza cálculos, conciliaciones, validación y XBRL sobre toda la población. El modelo también ve las instrucciones y valores necesarios para usar las herramientas: al crear el caso, razón social, identificador fiscal, domicilio, período y configuración; al ingerir, ruta o nombre local y opciones; después, mapeos e importes revisados, anexos, respuestas, textos, problemas y declaraciones de aprobación. Las respuestas operativas son resúmenes compactos.

Las lecturas específicas de mapeos y cuestionario y las vistas profesionales se solicitan por separado; las colecciones paginadas devuelven como máximo 500 registros por página con desplazamiento, total e indicación de más páginas. Según la vista pueden aparecer metadatos y anclajes documentales, filas PDF y OCR, códigos y descripciones de cuentas, saldos actuales y anteriores, mapeos, conceptos taxonómicos, hechos y totales, anexos, preguntas y respuestas, hechos aceptados, textos actuales o anteriores, problemas, decisiones, aprobación y hashes de artefactos. La lectura del workpaper solo devuelve metadatos de aprobación, hash del snapshot, referencia opaca y metadatos del artefacto, nunca el contenido del snapshot, rutas de almacenamiento ni bytes. Para el razonamiento semántico rigen límites más estrictos: de 1 a 50 cuentas para mapeo; como máximo 20 elementos por colección para un PDF en revisión; las primeras 20 cuentas y hasta 50 selectores exactos adicionales en total para la aplicabilidad; hasta 50 preguntas activas; una sección de memoria con evidencia aceptada vinculada por el paquete de reglas y hasta 50 referencias adicionales; 20 textos anteriores y 20 actuales para comparar; o 20 detalles por colección o 20 problemas exactos para guía y validación. Los selectores exactos y la paginación mantienen accesible todo el expediente; cada paquete registra tarea, selección, límites, recuentos y hash. Razón social, identificador fiscal, domicilio, tenant e identificador de enrutamiento se excluyen de los paquetes semánticos, no de los comandos operativos que los necesitan. El modelo no recibe automáticamente los archivos fuente, case.json ni el snapshot completo.

No hay anonimización ni seudonimización automática: descripciones, nombres e identificadores permanecen cuando lo exigen el significado contable, la prueba o la responsabilidad profesional. El modelo usa las mismas herramientas y límites. El modelo puede sugerir, pero no acepta filas PDF, hechos, mapeos, información, aprobación ni XBRL. Fuera del tratamiento por el modelo, los únicos destinos son investigación oficial sin datos del cliente, descargas OCR sin documentos y una carga TEBENI opcional elegida expresamente por el usuario.

Para el cierre de cuentas, el modelo también puede leer el origen de la contabilidad, los requisitos documentales, un borrador de solicitud no enviado, propuestas de debe/haber, diferencias entre balances de comprobación, decisiones y controles suspendidos. Las vistas solicitadas expresamente pueden devolver extractos completos de adjuntos UTF-8 CSV, Markdown, texto o JSON de hasta 64 KiB por archivo y página, con referencias y huellas; otros formatos o archivos mayores requieren una extracción cualificada. Los extractos pueden contener nombres y datos reales. Las propuestas no aprueban ajustes ni exclusiones y no envían solicitudes. La guía incluye como máximo 20 requisitos, 20 cuestiones abiertas y 20 dependencias, con los recuentos completos.

En el recorrido local CH-GE, separado del servicio OIC/XBRL descrito arriba, el modelo puede leer documentos seleccionados, identidad, saldos actuales y comparativos, mapeos, requisitos de notas, fuentes suizas y decisiones para preparar el borrador. El código comprueba hashes, cobertura de cuentas y conciliaciones sin llamadas de red. Este recorrido no usa los límites de paquetes OIC, no genera XBRL ni certifica la integridad legal.
fr: Le code traite l'intégralité des comptes ; le modèle voit les données opérationnelles demandées, tandis que le raisonnement sémantique utilise des paquets plus étroits.

Le code local importe toute la balance et les justificatifs sélectionnés, conserve lignes et références et exécute calculs, rapprochements, validation et XBRL sur toute la population. Le modèle voit aussi les instructions et valeurs nécessaires aux outils : à la création, dénomination légale, identifiant fiscal, siège, période et configuration ; à l'ingestion, chemin ou nom de fichier local et options ; puis mappings et montants revus, tableaux, réponses, textes, problèmes et déclarations d'approbation. Les réponses opérationnelles sont des synthèses compactes.

Les lectures dédiées des mappings et du questionnaire et les vues professionnelles sont demandées séparément ; les collections paginées renvoient au plus 500 enregistrements par page avec décalage, total et indication d'une suite. Selon la vue, elles peuvent contenir métadonnées documentaires et ancrages, lignes PDF et OCR, codes et libellés de comptes, soldes courants et antérieurs, mappings, concepts taxonomiques, faits et totaux des états, tableaux, questions et réponses, faits acceptés, textes courants ou antérieurs, problèmes, décisions, approbation et empreintes des artefacts. La lecture du workpaper ne renvoie que les métadonnées d'approbation, l'empreinte du snapshot, une référence opaque et les métadonnées d'artefact, jamais le corps du snapshot, les chemins de stockage ou les octets. Le raisonnement sémantique a des limites plus strictes : 1 à 50 comptes pour le mapping ; au plus 20 éléments par collection pour un PDF en revue ; les 20 premiers comptes et jusqu'à 50 sélecteurs exacts supplémentaires au total pour l'applicabilité ; jusqu'à 50 questions actives ; une section d'annexe avec les preuves acceptées liées par le rule pack et jusqu'à 50 références supplémentaires ; 20 textes antérieurs et 20 actuels pour la comparaison ; ou 20 détails par collection ou 20 problèmes exacts pour le guidage et la validation. Sélecteurs exacts et pagination gardent tout le dossier accessible ; chaque paquet consigne tâche, sélection, limites, nombres et hash. Dénomination légale, identifiant fiscal, siège, tenant et identifiant de routage sont exclus des paquets sémantiques, pas des commandes opérationnelles qui les exigent. Le modèle ne reçoit pas automatiquement les fichiers source, case.json ni le snapshot complet.

Il n'y a ni anonymisation ni pseudonymisation automatique : descriptions, noms et identifiants restent lorsque le sens comptable, la preuve ou la responsabilité professionnelle l'exige. Le modèle utilise les mêmes outils et limites. Le modèle peut suggérer, mais n'accepte ni lignes PDF, faits, mappings, informations, approbation ou XBRL. Hors traitement par le modèle, les seules destinations sont les recherches officielles sans données client, les téléchargements OCR sans documents et l'éventuel envoi TEBENI choisi explicitement par l'utilisateur.

Pour la clôture des comptes, le modèle peut aussi lire l’origine de la comptabilité, les besoins documentaires, un brouillon de demande non envoyé, les propositions débit/crédit, les écarts entre balances, les décisions et les contrôles suspendus. Les vues explicitement demandées peuvent fournir des extraits complets de pièces UTF-8 CSV, Markdown, texte ou JSON, jusqu’à 64 Kio par fichier et par page, avec références et empreintes ; les autres formats ou fichiers plus volumineux nécessitent une extraction qualifiée. Les extraits peuvent contenir des noms et données réels. Les propositions n’approuvent ni écritures ni exclusions et n’envoient aucune demande. Le guidage comprend au maximum 20 besoins, 20 questions ouvertes et 20 dépendances, avec les décomptes complets.

Dans le parcours local CH-GE, distinct du service OIC/XBRL décrit ci-dessus, le modèle peut lire les documents sélectionnés, l’identité, les soldes courants et comparatifs, les mappings, les exigences de l’annexe, les sources suisses et les décisions pour préparer le projet. Le code vérifie les empreintes, la couverture des comptes et les rapprochements sans appel réseau. Ce parcours n’utilise pas les limites des paquets OIC, ne génère pas de XBRL et ne certifie pas l’exhaustivité légale.
it: Il codice elabora l'intero bilancio; il modello vede i dati operativi richiesti, mentre il ragionamento semantico usa pacchetti più stretti.

Il codice locale importa l'intero bilancio di verifica e gli allegati selezionati, conserva righe e riferimenti ed esegue calcoli, quadrature, validazione e XBRL sull'intera popolazione. Il modello vede anche le istruzioni e i valori necessari per usare gli strumenti: all'apertura, ragione sociale, codice fiscale, sede, periodo e configurazione; all'ingestione, percorso o nome locale e opzioni; poi mapping e importi rivisti, prospetti, risposte, testi, problemi e dichiarazioni di approvazione. Le risposte operative sono riepiloghi compatti.

Le letture dedicate di mapping e questionario e le viste professionali sono richieste una alla volta; le raccolte paginate restituiscono al massimo 500 record per pagina con offset, totale e indicazione di altre pagine. Secondo la vista possono comparire metadati documento e ancoraggi, righe PDF e OCR, codici e descrizioni conto, saldi correnti e precedenti, mapping, concetti tassonomici, fatti e totali di bilancio, prospetti, domande e risposte, fatti accettati, testi correnti o precedenti, problemi, decisioni, approvazione e checksum degli artefatti. La lettura del workpaper restituisce solo metadati di approvazione, hash dello snapshot, riferimento opaco e metadati dell'artefatto: non il contenuto dello snapshot, percorsi di storage o byte. Per il ragionamento semantico valgono limiti più stretti: da 1 a 50 conti per la mappatura; per un PDF in revisione al massimo 20 elementi per raccolta; per l'applicabilità delle informative i primi 20 conti e fino a 50 selettori esatti aggiuntivi complessivi; fino a 50 domande attive; per la nota una sezione con evidenza accettata collegata dal rule pack e fino a 50 riferimenti aggiuntivi; per il confronto 20 testi precedenti e 20 correnti; per guida o validazione 20 dettagli per raccolta o 20 problemi esatti. Se serve altro, selettori esatti e paginazione mantengono raggiungibile l'intero caso; ogni pacchetto registra attività, selezione, limiti, conteggi e hash. Nome legale, codice fiscale, sede, tenant e identificativo di instradamento sono esclusi dai pacchetti semantici, non dai comandi operativi che li richiedono. Il modello non riceve automaticamente i file sorgente, case.json o lo snapshot completo.

Non c'è anonimizzazione né pseudonimizzazione automatica: descrizioni, nomi e identificativi restano quando servono al significato contabile, alla prova o alla responsabilità professionale. Il modello usa gli stessi strumenti e limiti. Il modello può suggerire, ma non accetta righe PDF, fatti, mapping, informative, approvazione o XBRL. Fuori dal modello, le sole destinazioni sono ricerche ufficiali senza dati cliente, download OCR senza documenti e l'eventuale upload TEBENI scelto esplicitamente dall'utente.

Per la chiusura dei conti, il modello può leggere anche origine della contabilità, requisiti documentali, bozza non inviata di richiesta, proposte Dare/Avere, differenze fra bilanci di verifica, decisioni e sospensioni. Le viste richieste esplicitamente possono restituire estratti completi di allegati UTF-8 CSV, Markdown, testo o JSON fino a 64 KiB per file e per pagina, con riferimenti e impronte; altri formati o file più grandi richiedono un’estrazione qualificata. Gli estratti possono contenere nomi e dati reali. Le proposte non approvano rettifiche o esclusioni e non inviano richieste. La guida al workflow include al massimo 20 requisiti, 20 questioni aperte e 20 dipendenze, con i conteggi completi.

Nel percorso locale CH-GE, separato dal servizio OIC/XBRL descritto sopra, il modello può leggere documenti selezionati, identità, saldi correnti e comparativi, mapping, requisiti delle note, fonti svizzere e decisioni per preparare la bozza. Il codice verifica hash, copertura dei conti e quadrature, senza chiamate di rete. Questo percorso non usa i limiti dei pacchetti OIC, non genera XBRL e non certifica la completezza legale.

security_controls.control: The deterministic importer accepts only bounded regular CSV, XLSX, or PDF files and rejects symbolic links. CSV/XLSX intake rejects duplicate account identifiers, headers that collide after alias normalization, non-finite or exponent monetary lexicals, ambiguous double signs, and operationally unbounded values; XLSX opens without macros or external-link resolution. PDF intake extracts only page/table/text or OCR geometry into a non-authoritative candidate and retains the source SHA-256.

A readable or scanned PDF extraction cannot create canonical entries. It remains PENDING_REVIEW with candidate-hash-bound page methods and table coverage plus page, table, row, source column, bounding box, method, raw value and OCR confidence. Any page still requiring OCR, incompatible table, or unaligned row blocks the whole source; pages without detected tables require exact reviewed non-accounting dispositions. An authenticated professional must accept the exact candidate hash, confirm all four review declarations, supply or confirm a one-to-one accounting-column mapping, and record corrections and exclusions with reasons. A non-account exclusion requires zero or blank selected monetary fields; a non-zero summary exclusion must name accepted account rows and reconcile every monetary field within parser tolerance. Only then may reviewed rows pass through the existing Decimal/parser controls. Bounded model context may explain extraction issues but cannot accept, correct, exclude, or promote rows; parser-convention confirmation remains a separate gate.

Every mutating command requires the current revision, an approval binds the exact canonical snapshot and input manifest hashes, and a later mutation invalidates and archives that approval before a new revision is created.

The catalogue builder requires the expected official-package SHA-256 and bounded traversal-safe ZIP extraction, distinguishes reportable items from tuples and non-item schema concepts, and preserves tuple and relationship metadata. Export reads the catalogue once, requires the exact catalogue hash approved during local review, re-renders from those captured bytes, requires byte identity with the approved XBRL candidate, emits the exact checksum-verified preview bytes shown to the reviewer, and writes checksums for every artifact. Review and export artifacts are written to a sibling staging directory and published atomically only after completion, so a failed job does not leave a partial destination.

Before approval, the current substantive case is rendered through one captured checksum-bound catalogue payload and the pinned Arelle interface runs structural and XBRL 2.1 calculation validation with offline internet connectivity. The candidate must remain byte-identical across validation; candidate, catalogue, package, and report hashes enter the approval snapshot, and substantive changes invalidate that review.

The prior-instance parser accepts only bounded regular local files, rejects symbolic links and document type declarations, disables entity and network resolution, requires one schema reference, validates context periods, unit definitions and XML-decimal monetary values, and checks the entity identifier, comparative period and EUR reconciliation unit before attaching source-anchored facts. Explicit dimensions, canonicalized typed dimensions, tuple ancestry, segment/scenario placement and context-fact groups are retained without executing or remotely resolving supplied XML.

The mapping-memory store rejects a tenant identifier mismatch and symbolic links, hashes the client key within the tenant, gives client mappings precedence, requires explicit tenant-wide scope, verifies the approved snapshot hash, and stores classifications without historical amounts or source anchors.

Movement and cash-flow schedules accept only normalized decimal fields with observed or user-confirmed source references; exact opening, closing, maturity, secured-payable, inventory movement, statement, reclassification, and cash-change failures remain blocking instead of being repaired by assumptions. Inventory costing method and valuation basis remain free professional conclusions; net-realisable-value, obsolescence, count evidence, and pledged-stock review fields close only with explicit terminal professional states. The inventory statement line must be backed exclusively by reviewed mappings to the selected form's inventory concepts, while cross-class reclassifications remain possible when the exact movement and opening/closing statement tie-outs reconcile.

A deployment-controlled checksum-locked rule pack selects the official presentation roots permitted for each form and schedule family. Every normalized schedule cell requires a reviewed exact-concept binding or reasoned omission; monetary values permit only explicit sign multipliers, text facts use one exact source, and role-specific tuple paths allow repeated reviewed rows without flattening their structure. Matching primary facts are reconciled instead of duplicated, and repeated inputs, uncovered cells, all-omitted table routes, contradictory facts and out-of-bound concepts fail closed.

Trial-balance and schedule XLSX intake rejects path traversal, encrypted ZIP members, macros, external links, suspicious compression, oversized expanded packages, more than 20,000 rows, and formulas without trusted cached values; imported schedule cells retain exact source anchors.

The writable service derives tenant, actor, roles, and originating interface from the authenticated host environment rather than mutation payloads; tenant-scoped paths, capability checks, time-limited support grants, file locks, revision checks, and idempotency records gate every operation. Source and returned-report reads are confined to a deployment-configured input root; taxonomy paths and MCP/HTTP statutory and disclosure rule packs are deployment configuration rather than request data; explicit studio-admin migration accepts only identifiers resolved from the controlled bundled registry; and review/export destinations reject symbolic links in every existing ancestor component.

Conversational and worker ingestion require a host-configured scanner command expressed as a JSON argument array and executed without a shell. Parsing proceeds only after a CLEAN verdict; pre/post-scan size and SHA-256 must remain stable, and the engine, signature version, timestamp, document identifier, size and checksum are persisted as an audited receipt.

Only reviewer and read-only-auditor roles may issue idempotent artifact grants. Grants last 30 to 900 seconds, are HMAC-signed by a deployment secret, disclose no storage path, bind tenant, case, file and approved manifest checksum, reject non-canonical Base64URL encodings before signature verification, and require safe-path, size and checksum verification again at redemption; issue and download events are audited.

The service has no implicit retention period. An owner-approved host value from 1 to 3,650 days enables studio-admin archiving while preserving approved artifacts. Purge requires the exact case revision and an elapsed recorded cutoff, removes only the validated tenant/case directory, and leaves a checksum-protected idempotent tombstone with hashes and accountability metadata rather than source content.

Long-running work may be persisted only as checksum-verified, tenant-scoped jobs created by an already authorized requester. Execution is reserved to the internal SERVICE_WORKER role, retries replay through the mutation idempotency ledger, compact status omits source-bearing payloads, and an intervening case revision makes unapplied work terminally STALE. Taxonomy builds accept no request-selected package, registry, path or entry point. Host semantic invocation receives only a minimum-context packet, runs outside the mutation lock, stores the exact response for retry recovery, and may record only a MODEL_SUGGESTED result.

The review-view service authorizes every tenant-scoped read, caps collection pages at 500 records, returns compact preview and artifact resource identifiers rather than file bytes or arbitrary host paths, and excludes the immutable approval snapshot payload from the approval/export view. Dedicated mapping and questionnaire reads use the same maximum with explicit pagination. The workpaper read verifies the snapshot hash but returns only approval/hash/resource and exported-artifact metadata, not the snapshot body.

The optional HTTP adapter accepts authentication only as a host-injected RequestContext, never from tenant or role request fields. Case creation rejects request-selected statutory rule packs; mutations require an Idempotency-Key and current If-Match revision; stale writes return a conflict; and read routes return structured resources rather than source or artifact bytes.

Canonical case and idempotency JSON records and their SHA-256 sidecars are written through bounded non-symlink temporary paths and every load verifies the sidecar before parsing. Missing, malformed, mismatched, or symlinked record/checksum pairs fail closed.

Semantic tasks receive the same bounded packet builders in Codex and Cowork. Mapping is capped at 50 exact accounts; disclosure activation starts with 20 accounts and accepts at most 50 exact optional selectors; questions are capped at 50; narrative uses rule-linked accepted evidence plus at most 50 exact selectors; prior-year collections and workflow-guidance collections are capped at 20; and issue explanation accepts at most 20 exact issues. Packets mark document content as untrusted, omit direct entity identity and out-of-band routing identifiers, carry a SHA-256 context receipt and counts, and provide lossless selector or pagination follow-up. Catalogue-only references are not citeable evidence. Strict output schemas and evidence-reference closure keep mapping, narrative, disclosure and workflow outputs MODEL_SUGGESTED until a separate professional decision. Raw case/source fallback is prohibited when packet tooling is unavailable.

Selected-form primary-statement requirements come only from checksum-bound official presentation and calculation relationships plus a versioned host-controlled policy. Every absent current or comparative leaf requires an explicit professional zero or not-applicable decision and reason; bounded model guidance may explain gaps but cannot create facts, confirm absence, derive authoritative totals, or make incomplete coverage exportable.

A user-supplied TEBENI report is accepted only as a bounded local regular file after local validation and approval, checksum-recorded as a non-authoritative external result, and attached without modifying or invalidating the approved accounting snapshot.

Approved client-history memory is tenant- and client-key scoped and retains only the selected form, accepted answer decisions, accepted narrative text, and recurring rule identifiers; it excludes direct identity, current amounts, and source anchors, and every future suggestion remains unconfirmed or stale until reviewed again.

Additional text, monetary, dimensional, and nil facts require exportable evidence status and exact source or derivation provenance; model-suggested states cannot be recorded, dimensional QNames are validated, and nil output requires both a professional reason and a catalogue concept that explicitly permits nil.

Structural blockers cannot be overridden; professional overrides are limited to HIGH issues and bind the exact issue fingerprint and reviewer reason. Material audit events record tenant, case, revision, actor, originating interface, and before/after content hashes.

The Geneva adapter requires a running Studio Archive context and exact imported source hashes, complete one-to-one reviewed mappings and balanced current/prior trial balances. Decisions bind the workflow, client, engagement, exact proposal and arithmetic. Outputs are content-addressed private drafts, never statutory approval or filing-ready artifacts. The Italy-specific authenticated service and XBRL controls do not apply to this local adapter.

The bridge authorizes case reads through the existing service context, requires the exact current revision when supplied, bounds views and context payloads, rejects unknown case source references and requires signed expiring UI tickets for issue review. The existing reviewer-role, case/run binding and idempotency checks remain authoritative.

The authenticated case service requires reviewer authority for closing decisions and a distinct actor for adjustment approval. Every mutation is revision-bound and idempotent. Closing decisions form a verified append-only hash chain binding actors, roles, evidence hashes, reviewed proposals and screened versions. Replacement accounts cannot become canonical without exact per-account reconciliation and professional screening; suspended controls and open professional issues block existing validation and approval.

Area planning requires exact complete account coverage, registered evidence and separate reviewer confirmation bound to the selected OIC checksum and the retained proposal hash. Exact source quotes and periods are checked before accepting interpretation proposals; prior-only sources cannot confirm current applicability. Source revisions and per-area dependency hashes reopen affected controls while retaining a verified append-only review chain. Model-facing pages refuse payloads above 64 KiB; native source views return exact bounded excerpts without arbitrary path reads. Private workbook output rejects stale revisions, symlink destinations, large cells and oversized downloads; all untrusted Excel cells are literal strings rather than formulas or links.
The OCR model-prefetch child receives the shared host/runtime environment allowlist plus its explicit module directory, model cache and installation guard, rather than unrelated user tokens and keys.

model_processing.destination: OpenAI model processing used by Codex
Anthropic model processing used by Cowork

external_boundaries.content: Published shared package names and version constraints plus ordinary package-index request metadata. No client files, prompts, case data, credentials, or generated work are sent by this runtime installer.
controls: Only published shared core and explicitly selected OCR recipes are installed; package names are never derived from client material or prompts.

Host network denials stop package retrieval. Retry only the same declared setup after the host user or administrator authorizes registry access; never change host network settings or use an alternate installer to evade a denial.

Readiness probes the managed CPython 3.12 interpreter locally with isolated Python and site loading disabled, checks completed installation metadata, then checks the selected declared package versions and component imports in that interpreter. Recipe revisions, backend bytes and historical platform labels do not block a compatible environment. Compatible reuse leaves installation receipts unchanged; actual missing or incompatible dependencies require serialized repair.
All three products and their modules use the same environment. Optional OCR requires approval and is then retained in that environment. A shared environment is not a boundary between client matters.
external_boundaries.destination: Python Package Index (PyPI) or the package index configured for the active Python interpreter
external_boundaries.purpose: Prepare the published shared Vera, Clara and Lucia core requirements and explicitly approved optional OCR in one user-scoped Python 3.12 environment per operating-system host.
external_boundaries.retention: Packages remain in one fixed user-scoped environment outside plugin source and client folders until explicitly removed. The default location is ~/.local/share/mparanza/runtime/venv on macOS and Linux, and LOCALAPPDATA/mpr/venv on Windows; MPARANZA_RUNTIME_ROOT may override the parent. Enabled OCR remains enabled across later core updates. Package-index request-log retention is controlled by the configured index. Failed updates invalidate the readiness receipt and require repair before execution; this shared environment has no retained generations.

external_boundaries.content: The fixed CPython 3.12 version request, operating-system and architecture selection, and ordinary download request metadata. Setup does not read client files or add prompts, case material or generated reports to this request.
controls: Use an installed CPython 3.12 when available; otherwise use uv or automatically download the published uv 0.12.10 wheel, verify its pinned SHA-256, and provision private CPython 3.12 without changing system Python or shell profiles.
Probe the selected interpreter before creating the dependency environment; never fall back to executing workflows with another Python minor version.
A failed download or interpreter probe stops setup; existing environments and client files remain intact.
external_boundaries.destination: PyPI files.pythonhosted.org for the pinned uv bootstrap, and Astral python-build-standalone CPython distributions on GitHub
external_boundaries.purpose: Provision the single supported CPython 3.12 interpreter when it is absent, automatically bootstrapping uv if needed
external_boundaries.retention: When uv must be bootstrapped, the bootstrap executable and private interpreter remain inside shared runtime storage until removed. Download request-log retention is controlled by the providers.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Vera/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis.
controls: Only closed technical transport schemas are accepted; unknown fields and arbitrary recovery commands are rejected.
The fixed HTTPS transport refuses redirects. Reporting failures retain the outbox and do not discard professional outputs.
The remote connector is independent of local command-process startup. If the host cannot expose/connect it, no successful report is claimed.
Only two built-in setup/preparation retries may execute automatically, once per remedy revision. Client documents, ACLs and security settings are not changed.
A published update is not recovery. The failed operation must actually execute successfully before that installation delivery closes.

Supplemental diagnostics require ownership of the original report and matching execution metadata; they are stored separately and cannot change the original report UUID, delivery status or remedy revision. Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.
Actionable remedies target an explicit original report. Each delivery uses its own applicable revision; a different report with the same generic signal does not inherit that remedy.

A cached actual connector status permits only the two fixed retries for an existing matching local receipt and latest report. It performs no direct HTTP polling or identity adoption. Missing local receipts cannot be fabricated to authorise a retry.

A helper success records readiness. Host AI verification of the original task and inputs is required for all recovered outcomes, including setup/startup. Delayed failures cannot reopen an already recovered episode.
Failed fixed retries retain complete stderr privately for semantic review. Raw recovery stderr is not automatically transmitted.

An explicitly selected MPARANZA_INCIDENT_DELIVERY=local-only setting blocks automatic client HTTP transport for this execution while preserving local evidence. Incident queues are durably marked and not automatically flushed later; this does not make model-provider processing local-only.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza HTTPS operational-incident API and Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
external_boundaries.purpose: Diagnose observed execution/setup failures, return installation-specific remedies and receive actual recovery outcomes
external_boundaries.retention: Local capability, pending reports and receipts persist outside client folders. The service retains incident, report, remedy and outcome records; no automatic deletion period is enforced. Status access is scoped by the opaque capability. Pending diagnostic pointers and raw stderr persist in the private incident directory until a matching actual recorded supplementation receipt is acknowledged; unsuccessful review or delivery retains them. Supplementation never replaces the original recovery episode or reopens recovered records. Recorded original/outcome receipts can acknowledge only their exact local queued UUID without replacing the local capability or saved connector identity. Remedy revisions are retained from the surviving migration revision onward; overwritten legacy revisions are not reconstructed.

security_controls.control: Setup validates package-relative selections and installs the published shared recipe. No package names or dependency instructions are accepted from client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unknown module, missing requirements file, invalid target, or failed dependency validation stops the helper instead of executing it in a partial environment.

security_controls.control: One fixed environment is located outside plugin source and client folders. An exclusive operating-system installation lock waits for running managed Python readers, which hold a shared lease through a startup hook. Setup removes the ready receipt before mutation and restores it only after pip check and component validation. Failed setup leaves execution unavailable until repair. Symlink roots, locks and metadata are rejected. The installer is launched from base Python to avoid self-deadlock. This lease is concurrency protection, not a security sandbox. Other historical environments are not automatically deleted. State metadata normally uses atomic replacement. Only EXDEV or Windows error 17 falls back under the same installer lock to a single-link regular-file write with full-byte writes and fsync. Failed writes attempt to restore existing metadata or remove a newly created file; the ready receipt remains invalid until setup succeeds. This fallback is local and does not add a recipient or payload.
security_controls.on_violation: A target creation or validation failure returns a bounded setup error and the requested helper is not run.

security_controls.control: The Windows archive launcher probes a callable interpreter and package entrypoint without changing aliases, registry, execution policy or client folders. The archive helper checks package readability before setup and supplies an explicit task UUID to every managed archive command. Recovery requires reconnecting the selected existing archive root; tasks do not silently adopt each other's configuration. Diagnostics return bounded package/startup status rather than client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unreadable package or invalid session stops before runtime setup and archive commands.

security_controls.control: For the six explicitly supported assured modules, the launchers verify the complete package inventory and stable regular-file bytes against the embedded build-generated SHA-256 index. Symlinks, reparse entries, special files, extra directories/files, missing or changed code and unstable reads stop preparation. Unchanged hardlinked package code is materialized into a fresh private OS temporary directory; each copied file is re-read and must have one physical link, then the unchanged component integrity validator must pass. The managed installation and aliases are not modified. The copy contains indexed product code/assets, not client documents, credentials, workflow reports or dependency environments. This local index detects package drift; it is not a publisher signature, a signed origin attestation or proof of installed-host acceptance. Successful code copies remain in OS temporary storage for normal OS cleanup. The root-level host .in_use directory is non-executable bookkeeping: only ASCII numeric, ordinary single-link regular marker files are excluded from the product inventory. Nested directories, links, reparse points and non-numeric names there are rejected. Marker contents are not read, executed, transmitted or included in a recovery copy; host markers and installed product files are not modified.
security_controls.on_violation: Preparation failures and host permission denials stop execution. A failed private copy is removed; no installation chmod/unlink/manual repair, alternate sandbox or relaxed component validation is permitted.

security_controls.control: The parent Vera launcher reports a negative exit code or 137/247 as forced termination. It writes execution_failure.json only inside the selected workflow context output directory or its normalization/sample subdirectories; without that matching context it logs only. The diagnostic stores workflow/run identifiers, exit status and an explicit statement that memory exhaustion is not established by the exit code. It makes no model calls or network requests.
security_controls.on_violation: A worker failure remains failure; diagnostic persistence errors are logged rather than converted into a success.

security_controls.control: The standalone Python bootstrap passes uv only declared host paths, locale, proxy, CA and cache settings, preserving original environment-name casing. Unrelated token/API-key variables and inherited UV_*, VIRTUAL_ENV, CONDA_PREFIX, PYTHONHOME and PYTHONPATH are excluded; private UV_PYTHON_* and UV_CACHE_DIR values are set by the bootstrap. The same environment is used for interpreter discovery and its local probe.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from every bootstrap child process.

security_controls.control: The built-in incident dependency-setup retry uses the shared host/runtime environment allowlist, named runtime/state locations and recovery recursion guard instead of inheriting unrelated user tokens and keys.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from the child environment.

security_controls.control: When the maintained launcher itself runs under Python -I -B, it restores only its own resolved scripts directory for sibling technical-diagnostic imports. It does not add the caller working directory. Helper execution, diagnostic retention and explicit incident delivery policy remain unchanged.
security_controls.on_violation: The maintained launcher must stop rather than resolving technical diagnostics from the caller working directory.

No altered file contents or professional files are read for this report. Native-host binding, when invoked, accepts a random host UUID and scoped capability plus an optional explicit native-app label at the same incident service. Only the host capability hash is retained server-side. Stable app-profile UUIDs are derived from host UUID and app label; reporter-instance UUIDs may be task-local and do not count physical computers, plugin copies or people. App grouping grants no additional client status or outcome access. Operator views retain each original report, supplement, outcome and retry event with its actual reporting owner and server receipt time; missing historical task identity is not reconstructed. The native stdio identity bridge verifies its indexed entry, reporter, technical collector and product metadata, then executes an isolated temporary reporter snapshot using existing Python without installing dependencies. Its tool accepts only an existing reporter capability and sends host proof to the fixed register endpoint; it never returns the device key or copies the reporter key into the host identity file. Native broker version/session observations are retained separately from guest reporter and failure-worker observations. When native tools are not exposed in cloud Cowork, the saved remote connector continues to report under its distinct connection identity and physical-host linkage remains unknown; no device controls or folder permissions are expanded automatically. Native-helper failures return source-bound exception classes, errno or HTTP status, package-relative frames and developer-authored templates. Dynamic diagnostic values are not returned; unavailable capture is explicit. This bridge does not return raw stderr or device keys. The central recovery agent may request named technical evidence surfaces through a diagnostic-request remedy. The host AI replies with reviewed technical facts, the original report UUID and request revision. Original-task availability is represented by technical booleans, not task text, client identifiers or file contents. A resume remedy communicates a diagnosed correction to the existing authorized workflow; it does not carry executable code. Technical requests, response UUIDs, applicable revisions and their observed status are retained with the original episode. The central agent may implement and deploy incident-related software fixes through reviewed source and green CI under Fabio’s explicit recovery authorization; it does not receive professional case files or gain user-host permissions. Handled Studio Archive exceptions log their active traceback locally before returning the existing error JSON, allowing the same source-bound collector and host semantic review to retain their actual cause. The operator derives diagnostic publication, exact owner/report/revision receipt and reply states, the existing 15-minute deadline and reporting-owner last service contact from retained records. These delivery facts do not establish physical-host availability, diagnosis or original-task recovery. The operator also projects exact delivery, retry and original-task outcome evidence for all actionable remedy kinds, including software updates. Its 15-minute attention cadence is not an execution timeout. A local alert renderer uses technical incident facts and an AI-reviewed blocker, accountable next action, reason and scheduled check. An optional operator-maintained device label is accepted only with a recorded exact-device verification reference; it is not inferred from the recipient, OS or reporter identity. Rendered operator alerts may include opaque machine/case codes and a verified operator-device label, but no client contents, raw diagnostics, personal identifiers or credentials. The renderer neither sends email nor accesses the registry or client files. It rejects stale followup reviews and cannot assign an unreceived or overdue remedy back to the uncontacted Vera. Recovered labels require matching actual original-task success evidence; incomplete historical bindings remain unknown. The shared API also exposes a separate public workflow-testing endpoint: an allowlisted map of pipeline IDs to testing levels and baseline metadata, without incident details, computer IDs, run IDs or user feedback. Its reset is operator-only and does not change incident records. Native workflow transport supplies the same existing host proof during registration when it is available. The shared managed launcher also reports handled PDF recovery failures and subsequent attempts for journal-sampling and journal-bank-reconciliation. It projects fixed strategy/check identifiers, pass/fail/replay flags and attempt/readable-row counts only; PDF text, amounts, paths, adapter code and free-text rationale remain local. Supplements reuse the original report identity across process sessions and cannot certify original-task recovery. Other products carry the shared implementation but do not expose these journal workflows. Bank PDF inspection failures and subsequent corrections are linked per source, independently of journal failures. The bank source digest used in the episode key stays in local reporting state and is not added to transmitted evidence. Other bank statements cannot inherit that extraction recovery. The same native bridge also exposes the fixed task-usage operations documented by the workflow-usage service, with a verified usage-client/catalogue snapshot and task-scoped persistence. Those operations use the existing installation/computer capabilities internally and do not accept credentials, paths, commands or client documents. Error results include SQLite symbolic error codes where available; no raw database contents or diagnostic values are returned. A separate local execution service accepts a published component helper, its argument list, an idempotent job UUID and the retained usage-task UUID. It verifies an indexed code snapshot and invokes the existing managed runtime, without accepting shell expressions or external executable paths. Arguments, complete helper stdout/stderr, job status and cancellation evidence remain in private local execution storage; these can contain case data and are not included in incident HTTP payloads. On a result request, the helper output and status enter the selected host model context through the normal recorded output boundary. Internal collection of stdout is not counted as a model send. Existing subordinate-worker submissions keep their own recording boundary. Native cancellation reads the local OS parent-process graph only to terminate that job and descendants; the graph is neither returned to the model nor uploaded. Native execution and the fixed incident identity/usage broker are separate services.
